ideas.description: Explore. Start from the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe (I001) and change only the training resolution schedule. For the first 50% of steps, each augmented 32 px batch is downsampled to 24x24 with F.interpolate (bilinear, antialias=False) after flip, translate and cutout. The remaining steps stay at 32 px. The whitening conv and the rest of the net are unchanged; the 2x2 patch whitening and maxpools work at 24 px, giving 3x3 final maps before the global pool. Keep the LR schedule tied to step count, not resolution. In build, compile and warm up both input shapes (24 and 32 px) on synthetic data so no recompile happens in timed train. Eval stays at 32 px only.
ideas.expected: Early epochs cost about 44% fewer FLOPs, so total time drops about 10-18% (about 0.8-1.4 s at ~8 s). Accuracy changes by -0.2 to -0.7 pp. If the drop is <= 0.3 pp, H3.2.1 is supported and some of the saved time can go into extra epochs. A drop > 0.6 pp, or a recompile stall showing up in timed train, refutes it for this budget.

structured_output.summary:
No uncertainty-committee forecasts came with the inputs, so I couldn't adjust or drop anything based on them. The queue keeps I002-I008 (7 queued) and adds one explore idea for H3.2.1, which brings it to 8.

New idea: progressive resizing, training the first half of steps at 24 px with both graph shapes compiled in build. It is the cheapest untested route to a time cut above 10% that doesn't depend on epoch tuning.

Exploit vs explore: 5 exploit ideas (I002, I003, I004, I005, I007) and 3 explore ideas (I006, I008, new H3.2.1).

Order of work: settle the epoch edge first (I001 running, then I002/I003). Then try the regularization retune (I005) and compile/CUDA graphs (I004). Then run width (I008) and resizing as explore bets.

Intentionally not added yet:
- H1.3.1 (whitening ablation): information only, removes a known-good component.
- H3.1.1 (proxy filtering): heavy to implement; wait for the feasible anchor.
- H4.2.1 (Muon): prior evidence already leans toward refuting it.

Tree maintenance: D001 and E000 show the template is a 0.1 s stub, so H2.1.1's 50-70 s baseline premise is false. Rewrite or retire it, and measure any GPU-pipeline gain against the first real recipe instead; I001 already uses a GPU-resident pipeline. Once I001 lands, a near-miss just under 0.753 should be combined with I005 (weaker regularization) at the same epochs before spending more epochs.
